title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering and workflow constraints, group-level safety). Prior work documents prototype intent→configuration systems and advocates verifier/validator stages, but artifact-grounded evidence quantifying generator→verifier→repair pipelines in a tightly controlled experimental design is limited [1],[2].

This study asks the preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not measure the effect of independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Detailed reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution bundle and deterministic reconciliation.
sections.related_work:
We surveyed the recent NetOps and AIOps literature to identify close antecedents and open gaps. Prior intent→configuration prototypes and task-bench evaluations illustrate feasibility of translating operator intent into device configuration but typically evaluate first-pass generation accuracy across independent samples or specialized datasets rather than paired repair effects with deterministic verifiers [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain generate→validate→repair work (program repair, test-in-the-loop synthesis) motivates guarded pipelines and bounded self-correction; those studies demonstrate that a bounded verifier with clear tests can materially improve correctness in software-engineering contexts, but the demonstrations are domain-specific and do not directly establish NetOps invariants coverage [4],[5],[6].

Survey and safety literature on agentic AI and LLM deployment emphasizes failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and recommends verifier gates, provenance, and constrained tool access; these conceptual findings motivated our guarded design and strict oracle definition but do not substitute for artifact-grounded verifier-backed experiments in NetOps [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap positioning. The supplied verified records show work on intent-driven generators and many proposals for verifier-like guardrails, but we found limited published evidence of preregistered paired designs that deterministically reuse the same initial candidate to isolate repair-only effects. That gap motivated the present experiment: to quantify whether a single verifier-triggered repair applied to an identical candidate meaningfully changes the all-invariant-pass rate under deterministic verification.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 prior to execution. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), allowed at most one automated repair call per task, and specified one confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The full preregistration and execution plan are archived and indexed by the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = bdfa0f64...e23d).

Task bank and deterministic selection. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The sampling_plan in the preregistration deterministically selects tasks by ordinal index (the adapter cycles through deterministic offsets as specified) and targets very_hard and extreme workflow patterns with multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules, and required per-task required_sequence fields. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies; manifests are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Inclusion/exclusion checks (token-normalized leakage detection and syntactic pre-checks) were performed before any model call; the archived run reports no preregistered exclusions.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared requested model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). That file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; hosted-model nondeterminism therefore remains a possible source of variability. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; provider accounting in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and model_calls_used = 201.

Deterministic verifier and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the oracle. The verifier deterministically parses candidate configurations, enforces per-device allowed-field constraints, tests required_sequence ordering constraints, evaluates group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up constraints), and checks dependency rules encoded in each task. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 iff all required invariants pass. Per-episode validator_trace artifacts include validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and violation_codes; these traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Paired semantics, missingness, contamination, and power plan. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for each pair begin from the identical initial candidate; any paired difference therefore arises solely from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The missingness_plan specified that persistent unparsable outputs would be treated as failures in a sensitivity analysis; in the archived run there were no persistent unparsables. The preregistered power plan targeted detection of a ≈10–15 percentage-point paired increase at N = 200 given mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%), but the realized baseline pass rate was substantially higher (199/200), changing realized power and placing inference into a discrete discordant-count regime.

Statistical tests and exact McNemar implementation. The primary confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar applied to discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). For clarity and reproducibility we report the exact binomial formulation used by the executor: let n = n10 + n01 and k = n10. Under H0 (no directionality) k ~ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p is computed as p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 - BinomCDF(k - 1; n, 0.5)} (with the conventional handling for k = 0). For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this yields p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(1;1,0.5) = 1.0, 1 - BinomCDF(0;1,0.5) = 1.0} → p = 1.0; the archived analysis artifacts record p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the absolute risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples using bootstrap_seed = 1729; this procedure and parameters are recorded in analysis_log.jsonl.

Reproducibility and archival artifacts. All provider traces, per-call metadata, task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), raw model responses (execution/responses/), scoring episodes (execution/scoring/), deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg), and the execution manifest are archived and indexed in the evidence bundle. The model_configuration.json records the declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null; the initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e...15ba). These artifacts provide the authoritative inputs for reanalysis with the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest reports started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent provider accounting. Provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and condition_counts = {shared: 200, guarded: 1}.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). analysis/condition_summary.csv records:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Using the exact two-sided McNemar binomial calculation described above yields p = 1.0 for the observed discordant counts. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. All numeric values above are identical to the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and the CSV artifacts).

Representative repair diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair count = 1). Archived validator_trace artifacts for the repaired pair (artifact prefix execution/scoring/task-000008-*) identify the failure as a multi-step required_sequence ordering violation on an extreme composite task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). The repair applied a small reordering patch aligning the generated commands to the task's required_sequence; post-repair validation_after.valid = true. The validator traces include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and violation_codes before and after repair; these artifact fields support the localized failure diagnosis.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination. The run recorded no excluded preregistered tasks (exclusions = []). The missingness_summary CSV shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing or failed episodes. contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged entries. The deterministic_reconciliation episode accounting and provider_call_audit (cache_miss_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0) support that every shared initial generation was freshly obtained and reused deterministically across the paired episodes.

Exploratory diagnostics by task difficulty. The archived task manifests permit exploratory breakdowns by difficulty pattern (very_hard vs extreme), required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. In the archived sample the single failed baseline episode (the repaired case) occurred on an extreme/very_hard composite task with the largest required_command_count observed among representative tasks. This artifact-grounded pattern is consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering and dependency interactions concentrate failure risk. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes per-condition rates and the bootstrap distribution used for CI construction.

Compact summary tables. Table 1 (Primary confirmatory results) and Table 2 (Execution and task accounting) are provided to summarize the artifact-grounded numeric outcomes and execution counts; their numeric entries are drawn directly from archived CSV artifacts and the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because each pair reused the identical sampled initial candidate, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on an identical candidate (a repair-only effect). This design intentionally excludes alternative guarded mechanisms (e.g., independently prompted guarded generations, constrained prompting, mult-sample selection). Readers should not generalize the present result to those other interventions without separate experiments.

Statistical regime and power implications. The preregistration targeted detection of moderate absolute paired improvements (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 under baseline assumptions near 45–65%. The actual baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those assumptions, producing low realized power to detect small absolute differences; with very small discordant counts the exact McNemar p-value is uninformative (p = 1.0 here), so the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] is useful to bound plausible effect sizes compatible with the data. In practice, extremely high baseline success rates constrain the inferential resolution for repair-only effects.

Operational implications and bounded claims. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach that the verifier could detect and the repair routine could correct. This supports a tightly bounded operational conclusion: in a deterministic synthetic task bank using gpt-5-mini and a well-specified deterministic verifier, a verifier-triggered bounded repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates. It does not imply that guarded repair will reliably fix semantic misinterpretations of intent, omissions revealed only by dataplane telemetry, or adversarially poisoned contexts. Broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-models, independent guarded generation semantics, live-device telemetry, adversarial contamination studies).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and the single initial generation per task mean the estimand measures only repair effects and is robust as such, but it does not address prompt- or sampling-related interventions. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not emulate live dataplane behavior; some operational faults require executing configurations in live or emulated dataplanes. External validity: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank limit generalization to other models, prompt templates, or production heterogeneity. Conclusion validity: with only one discordant pair observed, sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects remains large; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Recommendations grounded in artifacts. Future preregistered studies should (1) adopt independent first-pass generation semantics to estimate guarded-prompt or constrained-prompt effects, (2) evaluate multiple model variants to assess cross-model generality, (3) expand task diversity and include live emulation or dataplane tests to increase construct validity, and (4) include adversarial/contamination experiments to probe robustness to poisoned retrievals or malicious context. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived run (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, limited adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair under the exact binomial formulation described above. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
